course.title: Critical Thinking, Logic & Evidence
course.credential_boundary: 3 internal Khaemenes learning units; not institutional college credits.

modules.title: Claims, Questions & Definitions
modules.essential: How clear questions and definitions determine what can be reasoned about.

lessons.title: Claims, Questions and Testable Statements
lessons.focus: Distinguish assertions, questions, definitions and statements that can be evaluated.

lessons.title: Definitions, Boundaries and Ambiguity
lessons.focus: Test whether a definition is clear enough to separate examples from nonexamples.

lessons.title: Necessary, Sufficient and Relevant Conditions
lessons.focus: Separate what must be true, what is enough, and what merely happens to be associated.

modules.title: Logical Structure
modules.essential: How the form of an argument differs from the truth of its premises.

lessons.title: Premises, Conclusions and Argument Form
lessons.focus: Map an argument into reasons and conclusion.

lessons.title: Validity, Soundness and Strength
lessons.focus: Distinguish deductive validity from truth and inductive strength.

lessons.title: Converse, Contrapositive and Conditional Error
lessons.focus: Recognize valid and invalid transformations of conditional reasoning.

modules.title: Evidence & Burden of Proof
modules.essential: How the kind and quality of evidence should match the claim being made.

lessons.title: Evidence Types and Fit
lessons.focus: Match observations, documents, experiments, statistics, testimony and models to appropriate claims.

lessons.title: Burden of Proof and Extraordinary Claims
lessons.focus: Identify who is responsible for supporting a claim and how evidentiary demands change with stakes.

lessons.title: Absence of Evidence and Evidence of Absence
lessons.focus: Distinguish missing evidence from positive evidence against a claim.

modules.title: Counterexamples & Falsification
modules.essential: How one well-chosen case can expose overgeneralization or hidden assumptions.

lessons.title: Universal Claims and Counterexamples
lessons.focus: Use counterexamples to test broad claims.

lessons.title: Boundary Cases and Stress Tests
lessons.focus: Probe definitions and arguments at extreme or unusual cases.

lessons.title: Refining a Claim After Failure
lessons.focus: Revise an overbroad statement without abandoning defensible evidence.

modules.title: Fallacies & Rhetorical Distortion
modules.essential: How invalid reasoning and persuasive technique can create the appearance of support.

lessons.title: Relevance Fallacies
lessons.focus: Diagnose ad hominem, red herring, appeal to emotion and distraction.

lessons.title: Weak Induction and Overgeneralization
lessons.focus: Identify hasty generalization, cherry-picking and anecdotal substitution.

lessons.title: False Choice, Circularity and Loaded Framing
lessons.focus: Recognize false dilemmas, begging the question and premises hidden in wording.

modules.title: Causation & Explanation
modules.essential: How to distinguish correlation, mechanism, confounding and coincidence.

lessons.title: Correlation Versus Causation
lessons.focus: Avoid causal conclusions from association alone.

lessons.title: Mechanisms, Confounders and Alternative Explanations
lessons.focus: Generate plausible competing causes and identify missing variables.

lessons.title: Causal Evidence and Natural Experiments
lessons.focus: Compare observational and experimental evidence for causal inference.

modules.title: Probability, Risk & Uncertainty
modules.essential: How numerical uncertainty changes rational belief and decision-making.

lessons.title: Base Rates and Conditional Probability
lessons.focus: Use background rates to interpret evidence.

lessons.title: Relative Risk, Absolute Risk and Framing
lessons.focus: Translate risk claims into comparable forms.

lessons.title: Confidence, Uncertainty and Calibration
lessons.focus: Express belief with appropriate confidence rather than false precision.

modules.title: Sources, Testimony & Expertise
modules.essential: How to reason with information we cannot personally verify from first principles.

lessons.title: Expertise and Relevant Authority
lessons.focus: Distinguish relevant expertise from status or celebrity.

lessons.title: Consensus, Dissent and Minority Views
lessons.focus: Interpret agreement and disagreement without appeal-to-authority shortcuts.

lessons.title: Conflicts of Interest and Incentives
lessons.focus: Evaluate incentives without assuming that incentives automatically invalidate evidence.

modules.title: Argument Mapping & Counterargument
modules.essential: How strong reasoning anticipates objections and represents opposing views fairly.

lessons.title: Argument Maps and Hidden Premises
lessons.focus: Visualize premises, subclaims and assumptions.

lessons.title: Steelman, Objection and Reply
lessons.focus: Represent an opposing view in its strongest defensible form.

lessons.title: Disagreement Without Distortion
lessons.focus: Separate disagreement over facts, values, definitions and priorities.

modules.title: Decision-Making & Tradeoffs
modules.essential: How reasoning changes when choices involve uncertainty, costs and competing values.

lessons.title: Criteria, Constraints and Tradeoffs
lessons.focus: Make decision criteria explicit before comparing options.

lessons.title: Expected Value and Opportunity Cost
lessons.focus: Reason about likely outcomes and what is forgone.

lessons.title: Reversible, Irreversible and High-Stakes Decisions
lessons.focus: Adjust evidence thresholds to consequences and reversibility.

modules.title: Bias, Metacognition & Self-Correction
modules.essential: How thinkers monitor their own reasoning for motivated interpretation and blind spots.

lessons.title: Confirmation Bias and Selective Attention
lessons.focus: Notice when evidence search favors a preferred answer.

lessons.title: Anchoring, Availability and Salience
lessons.focus: Recognize common shortcuts that distort judgment.

lessons.title: Revision, Intellectual Humility and Error Logs
lessons.focus: Treat belief revision as a strength when evidence changes.

modules.title: Integrated Critical Inquiry
modules.essential: How logic, evidence, uncertainty and fair disagreement combine in public reasoning.

lessons.title: Case Audit: Competing Claims
lessons.focus: Compare multiple claims using a shared evidence rubric.

lessons.title: Evidence Brief and Reasoning Defense
lessons.focus: Write a concise evidence brief with counterargument and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Capstone Critical Inquiry Defense
lessons.focus: Defend a conclusion while identifying what would change your mind.

assessment.capstone: evidence brief + argument map + oral/written critical inquiry defense
